title: Coorg, Hampi and Mysuru (Batch 3)
selection: Batch 3. Coorg (5 sections), Hampi (6) and Mysuru (6) were thin. Adds who it's for, practical info, food, shopping, culture, local transport, tips and common mistakes, fuller overviews (pending review) and rewrites the three itineraries (moved here from karnataka.json). overview.text:
Coorg, officially Kodagu, is a hill district in the Western Ghats that people often call the 'Scotland of India' for its mist and green hills. It is India's biggest coffee- and pepper-growing district, and estates cover the slopes around Madikeri, the old British Mercara and the usual base.

The Kodava people give Coorg its character. Their warrior tradition produced Field Marshal K. M. Cariappa, they are the only community in India allowed to own certain firearms without a licence, and they have their own dress, food and festivals. Around Madikeri are Abbey Falls, Raja's Seat and the 1820 Omkareshwara Temple. Further out are Dubare's elephants, the Tibetan settlement at Bylakuppe, Talakaveri at the source of the Kaveri, and treks up Tadiandamol, the district's highest peak at 1,748 m. Visit from October to February for clear weather, or in the monsoon for full waterfalls.

overview.text:
Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, and around 1500 CE, Karnataka Tourism says, the world's second-largest city, a market for diamonds, pearls and silk. It fell after the Battle of Talikota. Today more than 1,600 surviving monuments are scattered across 4,100 hectares of granite boulders beside the Tungabhadra, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986.

Worship still continues at the Virupaksha Temple under its nine-tiered gopuram. At the Vittala Temple, the 56 musical pillars ring when struck, and the Stone Chariot is on the ₹50 note. The Royal Enclosure's Lotus Mahal and Elephant Stables blend Indo-Islamic design. Climb Matanga Hill or Hemakuta Hill for sunset, cross the river by coracle, or try the bouldering. Allow about three days, and come between October and February.

overview.text:
Mysuru lies at the foot of the Chamundi Hills, about 140 km south-west of Bengaluru, at around 770 m. It was capital of the Kingdom of Mysore for almost six centuries, from 1399 to 1947, and the Wodeyar kings left a city of palaces, gardens and wide roads. Mysuru Palace alone draws over six million visitors a year, and on Sunday evenings about 97,000 bulbs light it up.

The city's ten-day Dasara is one of India's great festivals. Mysuru also gives its name to silk saris, sandalwood, gold-leaf painting and Mysore pak. Beyond the palace are the Jaganmohan Palace art gallery, the Gothic St Philomena's Cathedral, Devaraja Market, the Chamundi Hills and, a short drive away, Tipu Sultan's island capital at Srirangapatna and the Brindavan Gardens. It makes a good base for Coorg and Nagarhole too.

days.distance: Madikeri to Dubare about 30 km; Namdroling at Bylakuppe about 34 km from Madikeri
days.driveTime: About 45 minutes to Dubare; Bylakuppe is near Kushalnagar on the way back

days.title: Tadiandamol
days.travel: Drive to the trailhead near Nalaknad Palace.
days.meals: Pack lunch and plenty of water.
days.distance: About 41 km from Madikeri to the peak area; the trek is about 14 km there and back from Nalknad Palace
days.driveTime: Allow the morning for the drive to Kakkabe; the trek takes most of the day

budget.assumptions: VacayOut has no verified current prices for Coorg homestays, taxis or entry fees. Budget for your own choices and check fees at each site.

booking.detail: Book ahead for weekends and the October–February season.
Arrive in the morning for the elephant sessions.

alternatives: In the monsoon: swap the trek for Iruppu Falls and the waterfalls near Madikeri.
Pilgrims: add Talakaveri, the source of the Kaveri.
tips: Carry rain gear outside the dry season.
Buy coffee and spices from plantation stores.

prep.title: Getting there
prep.body: Kannur airport (about 90 km) is closest; Mysuru Junction (about 120 km) is the nearest major railway station; buses run from Bengaluru, Mysuru and Mangaluru.

prep.title: Trek
prep.body: Wear trekking shoes and start early; carry water and snacks.

faqs.a: Madikeri is the usual base; plantation stays are scattered around it.

faqs.q: Can I swim at Abbey Falls?
faqs.a: No, bathing and swimming are not allowed.
October to February for clear weather; the monsoon for waterfalls.

itineraries.title: Hampi in 3 days: ruins, temples and coracles
itineraries.summary: The sacred centre and a Matanga Hill sunset, the Vittala Temple and a coracle crossing, then the Royal Enclosure and the museum.
itineraries.seoTitle: Hampi 3-Day Itinerary: Virupaksha, Vittala & Royal Enclosure
itineraries.seoDescription: Three days in Hampi: Virupaksha Temple, Hemakuta Hill and Matanga Hill sunset; the Vittala Temple and coracle ride; the Royal Enclosure, Lotus Mahal and museum.

plan.overview: Karnataka Tourism suggests about three days to do Hampi justice. This plan takes one zone a day, sightseeing early and late to avoid the midday heat.
plan.season: October–February is the recommended time; the Hampi Utsav adds dance and music.
plan.difficulty: Moderate: lots of walking and two short hill climbs

days.title: The sacred centre and Matanga Hill

stops.name: Virupaksha Temple
stops.note: Look for the inverted shadow of the gopuram.

stops.name: Hemakuta Hill and the monolithic Ganeshas

days.travel: From Hosapete Junction, about 13 km by road.
days.meals: Breakfast and dinner near Hampi Bazaar.
days.distance: Hosapete Junction to Hampi about 13 km; the sacred centre is walkable
days.driveTime: Short auto ride from Hosapete, then on foot

days.title: Vittala Temple and the river

stops.name: Vittala Temple and the Stone Chariot

days.travel: Cycle or walk along the river path, or take an auto.
days.distance: Within the Hampi site, along the river path
days.driveTime: On foot, by bicycle or auto — short hops

days.title: Royal Enclosure and the museum

stops.name: Hampi Bazaar and the Royal Enclosure

days.distance: Within the Hampi site — the royal centre is south of the bazaar

budget.assumptions: VacayOut has no verified current prices for Hampi stays, autos, coracles or monument tickets. Budget for your own choices and check fees at each site.

booking.detail: Buy at the ticketed monuments; check whether one ticket covers several sites.

alternatives: Climbers: give one morning to bouldering.
With a fourth day: Badami, Pattadakal and Aihole.
tips: Carry water and a hat; there is little shade.
Wear sturdy shoes for the hills.

prep.title: Getting there
prep.body: Hosapete Junction is about 13 km away; Vidyanagar airport, about 40 km away, has daily flights from Bengaluru and Hyderabad. Bengaluru is about 340 km away.

prep.title: Heat
prep.body: Even in winter, middays are hot. Plan sightseeing for early morning and late afternoon.

faqs.q: How many days do I need in Hampi?
faqs.a: About three, according to Karnataka Tourism.

faqs.q: Where does the coracle ride start?
faqs.a: From ghats near the Virupaksha and Kodandarama temples.

itineraries.title: Mysuru in 2 days: palace, Chamundi Hills and Srirangapatna
itineraries.summary: The palace, Jaganmohan gallery and Devaraja Market with a Sunday illumination, then Chamundi Hills, Srirangapatna and the Brindavan Gardens.
itineraries.seoTitle: Mysuru 2-Day Itinerary: Palace, Chamundi Hills & Srirangapatna
itineraries.seoDescription: Two days in Mysuru: the palace at opening time, Jaganmohan Palace, Devaraja Market and the illumination; then Chamundi Hills, Srirangapatna and Brindavan Gardens.

plan.overview: Time day 1 for a Sunday or public holiday so you see the palace lit up. Day 2 climbs the Chamundi Hills and heads out to Srirangapatna and the dam.
plan.start: Bengaluru (about 2–2.5 hours door to door by the expressway)
plan.season: October for Dasara; November–February for quieter, pleasant weather.
plan.difficulty: Easy; the Chamundi Hills steps are optional
plan.transport: Autos and cabs; train or road from Bengaluru

days.title: Palace, gallery and market

stops.name: Mysuru Palace
stops.note: Arrive at opening; no photography inside.

days.travel: Train or road from Bengaluru; Mysuru Junction is about 2 km from the palace.
days.meals: Masala dosa for breakfast; Mysore pak from a sweet shop.
days.distance: About 140 km from Bengaluru; Mysuru Junction is about 2 km from the palace
days.driveTime: About 2–2.5 hours door to door by the expressway

days.title: Chamundi Hills and Srirangapatna

stops.name: Brindavan Gardens
stops.note: Check the fountain-show timing on the day.

days.distance: Chamundi Hills about 13 km and Srirangapatna about 16 km from the city
days.driveTime: Short drives; allow 2–3 hours for Srirangapatna including travel

budget.assumptions: VacayOut has no verified current prices for Mysuru hotels, transport or entry fees. Budget for your own choices and check fees at each site.

booking.detail: Tickets at the gate; open daily 10 am–5:30 pm, last entry 5 pm.

alternatives: Wildlife: add a day for Nagarhole.
tips: Keep shoes and cameras for outside the palace.

prep.title: Getting there
prep.body: Fly into Bengaluru and drive about 3.5 hours, or take one of the daily trains to Mysuru Junction. Mysore Airport (about 10 km south) has a few domestic flights.

prep.title: Weather
prep.body: Summer is March–May and the monsoon June–October; November–February is most pleasant.

faqs.q: When is the palace lit up?
faqs.a: 7 to 8 pm on Sundays and public holidays, and two hours nightly during Dasara.

faqs.q: Can I take photos inside the palace?
faqs.a: No, photography is allowed only outside.

faqs.q: Is the Brindavan fountain show every evening?
faqs.a: Wikipedia says so, but check timings locally before you go.
